title: Meera Exports v. Global Commodities
text: The plaintiff, Meera Exports, claims damages for breach of contract against the defendant, Global Commodities, for failure to supply contracted goods on the agreed date. The defendant failed to deliver 500 metric tonnes of raw cotton as per the supply agreement. This caused the plaintiff to source the goods at higher market rates, resulting in losses. Under the law of contract, the measure of damages for breach of contract in a supply agreement is the difference between the contract price and the market price on the date of breach. The defendant's plea of force majeure due to floods was rejected as the defendant did not issue a force majeure notice as required by the contract and failed to prove the event. Breach of contract is established. The court awards damages of Rs 1,20,00,000 as the difference between market price and contract price. Additional damages for consequential losses are denied as they were not foreseeable. Consideration in the matter of costs is in favour of the plaintiff.
